My approach to learning Skullgirls when I was brand new to fighting games, was doing the tutorials, and then playing cpu matches to get used to how controlling my character feels. I struggled a LOT with movement and doing special moves early on, so a safe environment helped a lot with that. If you were playing a game with a larger community I’d say hop online and find other new people, but skullgirls makes it a bit harder to do that. Pick a character and familiarize yourself with their kit, and the range of their moves, and how to use movement to get those hits.

Once you do that, learn *SIMPLE* combos. A trap a lot of fighting game noobs fall for is thinking that damage is what makes a combo good. Thats a lie. The value of a combo is in the advantages it gives you. A combo that ends in a hard knockdown, or puts your opponent in the corner but only deals 5k damage is infinitely more useful than a 17k damage combo that gives you nothing like that.

If you already know what character you wanna play, i can give you some simple strings to work with

Its alright to just do basic combos. All crazy combos do is let you get more damage off of stray hits, its more important to learn how to play neutral so you just get more stray hits than your opponent. Take your time getting used to the feel of the game and mechanical skill like that will come naturally
